title: Version-locking & runtime negotiation shim for safe model rollouts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need a lightweight "version-locking" mechanism and a runtime negotiation shim that guarantees safe model rollouts across runtime and model version boundaries. Current routing can select newer model binaries onto older runtimes (or vice versa), which occasionally causes degraded responses or OOMs. This ticket defines the design, validation steps, and rollout gates for a compatibility-first rollout flow so product teams can pin routes to model+runtime pairs and rely on automatic graceful downgrades when incompatibilities are encountered.

Goals:
- Provide a simple pinning config for routes that binds a route to a model version and a runtime LTS channel.
- Implement a runtime negotiation shim that verifies compatibility at request time and applies a deterministic fallback policy if pairing is incompatible.
- Add rollout gates and automatic rollback criteria (latency, error-rate, quality regressions) for canary and staged rollouts.
- Expose clear observability (per-route pairing metrics, contact points for stuck fallbacks) and a migration path for customers using previous pin mechanisms.

Non-goals:
- Full orchestration of runtime upgrades (separate project).
- Rewriting the serving runtime; we only add a coordination shim and config schema.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Compatibility registry: a commit-backed dataset mapping model versions to minimum and recommended runtime channels (LTS or nightly). This registry is maintained by model-ops and release-engineering and published as a signed artifact.
2) Route pin config: a route-level declarative field (route.pin) where teams can specify either: 
   - "model_version": "mymodel@v2.3" and "runtime_channel": "lts-1" (strong pin), or
   - "model_version": "mymodel@latest" and "runtime_channel": "recommend" (loose pin).
3) Runtime negotiation shim: on request arrival, the router consults the compatibility registry and the route.pin; the shim will verify the runtime node's channel label vs. the desired channel and will accept, redirect, or apply fallback based on configured policy.
4) Fallback policies (configurable at route and org level):
   - fail_open: route continues to newer runtime if minor incompatibility only (not recommended for LTS routes).
   - fail_closed: reject requests and surface a 503 with instrumentation (recommended for high-risk changes).
   - graceful_downgrade: route is sent to a pinned older model variant that is compatible with node runtime (requires cached older model artifacts).
5) Rollout gates: stages at 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated checks at each stage for:
   - p50/p95 token latency increase threshold (default +30% p95),
   - server-side error rate > 0.5% absolute or 3x baseline,
   - downstream quality regressions as measured by prompt-set evals (optional hook).
If any gate fails, traffic is automatically routed to the previous stable pairing and an alert is created.

Configuration examples (proposal):
- Route-level pin (strong):
  {
    "route": "/chat",
    "pin": {
      "model_version": "redwood-chat@3.2.1",
      "runtime_channel": "lts-1",
      "fallback": "graceful_downgrade"
    }
  }

- Org-level default (loose):
  {
    "default_pin_policy": "recommend",
    "fallback": "fail_open"
  }

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (2 weeks): Compatibility registry prototype and signed artifact format; basic UI for engineers to view mappings.
- M2 (2 weeks): Router shim implementation with policy engine and per-request check; unit + integration tests.
- M3 (1 week): Fallback execution paths: graceful_downgrade and fail_open; add hooks to cache older model artifacts on nodes.
- M4 (1 week): Canary rollout orchestrator and automatic gate evaluations; metric definitions in Graphite/Prometheus.
- M5 (1 week): Docs, migration guide, and runbook; partner with model-ops for initial registry entries.

Testing & validation:
- End-to-end test harness that simulates mismatched pairs and verifies fallback paths and metrics.
- Synthetic load tests with mixed sequence lengths to validate latency SLOs.
- Prompt-set regression check integrated into rollout gates (small curated set of prompts; failure threshold configurable).

Observability (minimum):
- pairing.active: gauge (current model+runtime per route).
- pairing.fallbacks.count by reason (compat_version, oom, kernel_mismatch).
- pairing.rollback.events (tags: route, env, stage).
- route.latency.p95 and route.error_rate (existing) wired into gate checks.
- an alerting policy for repeated graceful_downgrade events (>5 in 1h).

Migration notes for existing customers:
- We will add a compatibility check and a lint that warns for routes that previously relied on implicit behavior.
- Provide a migration CLI to generate recommended pin values based on observed runtime usages over the past 30 days.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Missing older model artifacts on nodes prevents graceful_downgrade. Mitigation: add proactive caching during rollout planning and a preload workflow in Dedicated.
- Risk: Overly strict pins prevent benign upgrades. Mitigation: support a "recommend" mode and an explicit operator override.
- Risk: Complexity of policies leads to misconfiguration. Mitigation: sane defaults, UI validation, and preflight lints.

Success criteria (MVP):
- Route pin config accepted by router and enforced on 1% canaries.
- Automatic rollback triggers on injected latency/error regressions in canary runs.
- Compatibility registry populated for top 10 served model families.

Open questions:
- Should the compatibility registry be writable by model-ops only or a wider set of teams? (Prefer model-ops validation + sign-off.)
- How should we version the registry artifact to support rapid rollbacks? (Propose immutable signed artifacts and a tag-based latest pointer.)

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Route+Pinning+and+Runtime+Negotiation+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/781
- Registry proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-registry/tree/feat/signed-artifact

Next steps:
- Review with model-ops and runtime team (week of 2025-03-11).
- Spin up M1 branch and add basic registry consumer to the router.
- Create a small canary run with internal test model and runtime mismatch scenarios.
